title: Patchwork Asks — Priority Snapshot (May 2026)
short_summary: Quick synthesis of disparate customer asks from support, AM notes, and field interviews — grouped into small feature clusters and proposed priority lanes for product review.
body:
Context and goals:
- Goal: turn a noisy set of ~42 individual asks into 6 pragmatic product/engineering bets we can present at the May 21 product sync.
- Source mix: support tickets (18), AM call notes (12), post-demo survey micro-essays (7), and two enterprise discovery sessions.
- Observed signal: many asks are small, incremental, and overlap; there is risk of double-counting similar asks phrased differently ("improved SDK parity" vs "missing SDK feature for streaming").

Raw customer snippets (verbatim paraphrases):
- "We need lower tail latency for short-chat flows; batching is great but hurts interactive UX." — fintech startup
- "Can you expose a per-route token-cost breakdown in the console? Our finance team needs this to chargeback." — large SaaS
- "Private deployment: KMS integration is a blocker for procurement." — healthcare enterprise
- "When Dedicated scales up we saw transient 503s; autoscale policy seems aggressive." — adtech customer
- "Embedding recall drift — our rerank quality fell after a model swap; need a rollback shortcut." — content platform

Clusters (deduped, name + short description + vote count from field team):
1) Observability & cost transparency (vote: 18)
   - Per-route token + cost breakdown in Console
   - Chargeback export (CSV / invoice line items)
   - Quick ask: add token-per-call column to existing route table and a one-click CSV export

2) Latency SLOs for interactive flows (vote: 15)
   - Short sequence path: optimize for <=100ms p50 for sub-64 token responses (hosted tier)
   - Request for low-latency model variants and explicit routing policy in API
   - Quick ask: published perf profile for "short-chat" across top 3 models

3) Private deployment gating (vote: 12)
   - KMS/HSM onboarding checklist required by procurement (cloud + on-prem options)
   - Audit log export cadence and sample retention policy doc needed
   - Quick ask: a one-page checklist and a sample SOC-like data flow diagram

4) Dedicated autoscale stability (vote: 9)
   - Customers report transient 5xx during scale-up; want graceful draining/fallback policy
   - Suggest: add configurable cooldown + automatic fallback to lower-capacity model variant
   - Quick ask: short-term mitigation playbook for solutions engineers

5) SDK parity & streaming ergonomics (vote: 8)
   - SDKs missing streaming helper for reconnect/backpressure handling
   - Docs ask: patterns for client-side polling vs server streaming, examples in node/python
   - Quick ask: a streaming helper and a sample retry pattern by end of Q3

6) Eval/regression guardrails for embeddings (vote: 7)
   - Customers saw recall regressions after model rollout; want preflight eval harness + rollback path
   - Propose: per-customer canary evaluation window + automated rollback threshold
   - Quick ask: start pilot with 2 customers for canary eval automation

Cross-cutting themes noticed:
- Many small asks point to the same underlying need: visibility and predictable economics (observability, cost, chargeback). Instead of many small UI tickets, a single observability initiative would absorb ~40% of requests.
- Enterprise customers are conservative: procurement gating (KMS, SLAs, audit) is a recurring stopper for Private deployments.
- A single incident (scale-up 5xx) has catalyzed several Dedicated requests — operational stability is a high-multiplier fix.

Quick risk/benefit notes for product prioritization:
- Observability work is high customer value, relatively low engineering risk (mostly UI/exports + telemetry additions). High ROI for mid-market + enterprise.
- Latency SLOs require runtime effort and maybe model catalog tagging; higher cost but strategic for PLG motion targeting interactive apps.
- Private gating is sales-enablement work (docs + checklists) vs deep engineering (KMS integrations vary by cloud). Prioritize docs + checklist first.
- Autoscale stability is urgent for existing Dedicated customers (SLA risk). Needs SRE + runtime engineering work and a short-term solutions playbook.

Proposed 6-week plan (minimal viable scope for each cluster):
W1: Finalize requirements with PMs and SRE; pick 2 customers for pilot observability exports.
W2: Ship small Console change: per-route token column + CSV export (observability MVP).
W3: Publish "short-chat" perf profiles; coordinate with research to tag model variants.
W4: Deliver Private deployment one-pager (KMS checklist + sample diagram) and circulate to pre-sales.
W5: SRE + Runtime: implement cooldown knob and rollout a Solutions playbook for Dedicated customers.
W6: Begin embedding canary pilot with two customers, measure and define rollback criteria.

Open questions & asks for PM sync (May 21):
- Do we accept observability as a single multi-quarter initiative and reclass smaller asks as sub-features?
- What is product appetite for a new "low-latency" offering (pricing, SLA)?
- Can the Security/Compliance team produce a canonical KMS onboarding doc or should Solutions draft a first pass?
- Which two customers are highest-value pilots for embedding canary? (nominees: ContentCo, QFin)

Next actions (owner tag in-line):
- [Aisha] Prep a 5-slide summary for May 21 PM sync focusing on ROI, pilot candidates, and quick wins (slides + demo script).
- [Tomás] Pull the support ticket set and flag duplicates; link tickets to the clusters in Confluence (due 2026-05-18).
- [Priya] Draft the KMS/procurement one-pager and a sample architecture diagram (due 2026-05-19).
- [Leo] Draft solutions playbook for Dedicated scale-up incidents; collect recent incident logs and sample mitigation steps (due 2026-05-20).

Appendix: sample ticket references (support IDs and brief note)
- SUP-3421: request for per-route cost export — customer: BigRetail — assigned to AM
- SUP-3587: Dedicated 503s during scale — customer: AdWorx — SRE investigating
- CS-204: Private deployment KMS question — customer: HealthNimbus — sales hold
- SUP-3699: embedding recall drop after rollout — customer: ContentCo — awaiting eval artifacts

Notes to self:
- When summarizing to execs, lead with "observability buys time" — fixes here reduce incoming small asks and defer some costly runtime changes.
- Keep pilot scope tight: deliver something tangible in 2 weeks to maintain momentum.

End of doc.
